title: The Library's New Map: Comparing Old and New Access · 独立口语迁移
instructions: 先完成示范段的跟读诊断，再用不同人物、信息或立场录制自己的完整回答。示范与自由回答分别取证，服务未提供完整听音评阅时保持待评。
reference: The Westside Library is changing. Last year, the library had one main entrance and a single information desk. Today, it has three entrances and two help desks. The library is now more open and easier to enter. In the past, visitors walked to the back of the building to find the catalog. Now, a digital map stands near the front door. The map is more helpful than the old paper list. It shows every shelf and every room. If you compare the old building with the new one, you can see that the library wants to make things simple for visitors. The new entrances also mean that people do not have to walk through the whole building just to ask a question. This saves time, especially for people who visit the library for only a few minutes. The number of visitors is growing. In January, about 1,200 people visited the library each week. In June, the number was 1,800.
prompt:
Part 1
Do you often visit libraries?
What do you use libraries for?
Do you prefer paper books or digital maps?
Is your local library busy?

Part 2
Describe a library or a place you know that changed. You should say: where it is; what changed; how people use it now; and explain why the change is good or bad.

Part 3
Why do some libraries change their design?
How can libraries help older people?
Do you think digital maps are better than paper lists?
What will libraries look like in the future?
